finding.claim: update_doc calls can_edit() but ignores its boolean return value, so authorization is never enforced. Any caller can overwrite the body of any document. The sibling route update_title correctly uses require_edit(), which aborts with 403.
finding.source: PUT /doc/<doc_id> with JSON body {"body": ...}; doc_id comes from the URL. Attacker is any user who can reach the endpoint and is not the owner or an editor.
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] at docs.py:20 (write to another user's document)

trace.note: Route PUT /doc/<doc_id> has no auth decorator
Document is loaded by the request-supplied id with no ownership check
can_edit(g.user, doc) returns a bool that is discarded; there is no if/abort

finding.guards_checked: Checked for a decorator or before_request hook enforcing edit rights; none exists in the file. require_edit (docs.py:11) is the enforcing variant, but update_doc does not call it. The only guard on the path is the discarded can_edit result, so it enforces nothing.

verdict.guard_found: Only can_edit (docs.py:7-8) returns a bool; its result is discarded at docs.py:19. No decorator or before_request hook exists in the directory. require_edit (docs.py:11-13) aborts with 403 but is not called by update_doc.
verdict.reason: At docs.py:19 the bare call can_edit(g.user, doc) discards its bool, so docs.py:20 overwrites doc["body"] for any caller who reaches the route, unlike update_title which calls require_edit at docs.py:27.
